highlights: A redesigned Team workspace. The sidebar now lists Team overview and every group in your organization. Team overview shows what needs your attention under To do, and each group has its own page with People, Devices, and Keys & security tabs.

Share with your team in a few clicks: create a group, use Add person to give someone access by email, and protect the group's folders so everyone in it can open the files on their approved devices. People already in your Team get access right away; anyone else is invited and gets access as soon as they join.
Invite to Team lets you choose which groups a new member joins before they arrive. The app shows a one-time invitation code to send them, and they paste it under Joining an existing Team? to join.

Members & devices lists everyone in your Team, their groups, devices, and open invitations, with filters for devices that need approval, have not been verified, missed a key update, or have not been used for a while. From there you can revoke a lost device, add someone to a group, or remove them from the Team.

Removing someone's access now rotates the group's keys in the same step, so they cannot open files added afterwards. Key rotation shows its progress, checks devices beforehand, finishes automatically once members confirm or its deadline passes, and then moves your files to the new key on its own.

Start without an account. HybridCipher sets itself up on first launch, and a short Get started checklist walks you through saving a recovery kit, protecting your first folder, and opening it in Finder. Create an account later to use your files on other devices; the folders you already protected join it without being re-encrypted.

The new Mount Center shows mounted folders from every workspace and group in one place. Mount all or Unmount all at once, follow each folder's progress, choose which folders mount automatically, and folders left mounted when the app last closed are reconnected when it starts again.
important_changes: New devices are easier to set up. Devices waiting for approval or fingerprint verification are listed together under Devices to set up, and people can approve their own new device from another device they already trust instead of waiting for an admin.
A device you verify on one of your computers is now also trusted on your other computers, so you no longer need to verify the same device again on each one.
Before a key rotation, the app lists any device that has not been verified on this computer and offers Verify now, so the rotation does not stop partway through.
Folder status now shows which key your files are on, for example 57 of 66 files on the latest key, instead of only whether they are protected.
The app notifies you when this device is missing a key needed for some files, and when a group's keys have been updated.
Team administration is available only on a verified device. If the current device is not verified yet, the app explains how to verify it from a trusted device or confirm it with your password.

Manage your recovery kit in Settings. If you lose the kit file or its recovery key, make a new one there. You can also use a recovery kit to open files you protected on another computer without an account.
Protecting or removing protection from a folder now runs in the background with its own progress window. If a protected folder was renamed or moved, the app helps you locate it again.
The folder menu now includes Decrypt and remove protection, and actions that cannot be undone are clearly marked.

Account security is stronger: signing in on a known Mac needs proof from that device's key, or your MFA code if it has none. Authenticator codes, MFA backup codes, and password reset links now work only once, and sessions have a maximum lifetime after which you sign in again.

Settings → Advanced tools now includes Copy key diagnostics, a summary of this device's key status for support that names no files or folders. The app also keeps a local log file to help troubleshoot problems.
The built-in console now runs only HybridCipher commands, and the old file browser and command list have been removed. Protected folders, Mount Center, and the Team pages cover these tasks.
If Finder stops syncing a mounted folder, the folder says so and offers to reconnect it. When macOS privacy settings block Finder from reaching a folder, the app explains what to allow.
fixes: When a file disappears from a mounted folder without you deleting it, macOS now restores it from its encrypted copy instead of removing that copy.
Fixed Finder-backed protected folders failing to start for user accounts with very long names.
A folder that is still being prepared after sign-in now says so, instead of failing when you try to use it.
Files that are already encrypted are now recognized by their contents, not their names, so they are never encrypted a second time.
Fixed a leftover session from a previous run blocking sign-in when the app starts.
If this device's saved identity can no longer be read, the app now guides you through setting the device up again instead of failing.
Folder status shows No files indexed yet instead of 0% covered for a folder that has not been scanned.

highlights: Recover with code: sign in on a new Mac and use your account password plus your saved encryption recovery code to restore your encryption keys and fully trust the device, with no email code or approval from another device needed.

Files encrypted by older versions of the app now appear in Finder as soon as a protected folder mounts. Opening one asks for your consent first instead of failing the mount, and other files stay available while you decide.
Conflict Review now works for Finder-backed protected folders on macOS, so you can compare and resolve conflicting copies from inside the app.
important_changes: The Personal workspace now always uses your account's default group. When that group is missing or cannot be identified, the home screen explains why and offers Recover with code, Repair Personal workspace, Check status, or Open Devices.
After recovery, the app reports device trust and encryption-key readiness separately and tells you exactly what remains, such as finishing Personal setup or getting newer keys from a trusted device.
Recovery backups created by older versions need a one-time upgrade with an email code, authenticator code, or MFA backup code. After that, your saved recovery code works on its own.
To keep recovery backups consistent, older app versions can no longer update them. Update the app on all of your devices to keep backups current.

A protected folder's details now list its older-format files. Open each one to check it, then upgrade one or all of them to the current format. Files are also upgraded the next time you save them, and an exact encrypted backup of each original is always kept.
Mounting continues in the background as soon as it starts. Close the progress window at any time; the folder shows a Mounting indicator until it is ready.
Settings now shows Open Team workspace for accounts that have already activated Team. Other accounts still see Activate Team.
When a protected folder is removed from Finder, macOS now preserves any edits that had not finished syncing. If any are rescued, the app opens their folder in Finder.
fixes: Fixed a case where recovery fully trusted a device but left the Personal workspace without a default group, blocking folder enrollment.
Fixed a background refresh that could interrupt Repair Personal workspace while it was running.
Fixed saving and renaming files inside nested subfolders of Finder-backed protected folders.
File names are now kept exactly as stored whenever macOS allows them. Unsafe characters are replaced only when necessary, so files still map back to the right encrypted source.
Device approval and revocation now report an expired authorization clearly and ask you to check your Mac's date and time when its clock is far off, instead of failing with a generic error.
Fixed expanded sections in a folder's details, such as Details for older files, collapsing every few seconds during background status refreshes.

highlights: The Personal workspace on macOS now focuses on your files and devices, with fewer Team controls. Activate Team remains available in Settings.

Device management is safer: the app explains when your current device needs approval or fingerprint verification before it can manage other devices, and guides you through confirmation when recovery is needed.
Workspace setup and device status refresh more reliably after approval or verification, clearing obsolete waiting notices and preventing completed actions from being retried.
important_changes: Device approval, verification, and revocation controls now reflect what your current device is allowed to do, with clearer guidance when an action is unavailable.
Switching accounts or workspaces prevents an earlier action or its Retry button from affecting your current workspace.
fixes: Failed Team activation leaves the Personal workspace available instead of exposing incomplete Team controls.
Retry disappears when an action succeeds, helping prevent accidental repeats.
Approval and verification refresh the workspace and device state, removing stale setup messages without repeatedly restarting setup.
Removing the device you are using first checks that protected folders can close safely. If pending work prevents a safe shutdown, device removal stops so you can resolve it first.

highlights: Fixed the "Legal documents unavailable" startup error affecting the macOS 0.1.6 release. The bundled Terms of Service and Privacy Notice now load from the correct location, so affected users can accept them and continue into the app.

Builds configured with the service's Team verification key support activation-code setup, workspace switching, member and invitation management, and clearer access status. Temporary builds without this key support Personal folders; Team activation and writes are unavailable.
Removing a protected folder now lets you choose to keep its files encrypted or decrypt them, with a warning before plaintext could reach cloud storage.
important_changes: Protected folders show an Unmounting indicator in the sidebar and folder details while the safety check and shutdown run, and prevent repeated unmount requests.
Devices → This device now offers Show fingerprint and Copy. Device verification explains where to find the fingerprint and accepts it with or without spaces.
Team write access is checked before macOS File Provider mutations. When Team access expires or is unavailable, protected edits are blocked and pending edits are preserved for recovery.
Team administration requests can be queued offline and retried after reconnecting, with clearer workspace, member, and invitation controls.
macOS releases now bundle the macOS release-note catalog separately from Windows, and release packaging uses an explicit destination for the legal documents.
fixes: Resolved the legal-document packaging path mismatch that could block first launch in macOS 0.1.6 even though the documents were included in the installed app.
Home now waits for session recovery before making authenticated requests, refreshes after successful background renewal, and retries unknown device or MFA status after a silent session refresh.
Logout, quit, and update flows require a safe protected-folder shutdown before proceeding, helping preserve pending work.
Temporary login keeps session keys in memory without creating an automatic-unlock cache.
The Settings window closes after a successful logout or session-expiry transition.
Older-file notices disappear when no older files remain; remaining format limitations and encrypted-original locations are available under Details.
Folders removed from Personal protection can be enrolled again into a Team workspace while preserving their history, and ownership failures are displayed correctly.

highlights: Moving a file or folder to the Trash from Finder now removes it from your protected folder instead of failing to sync.
The desktop app is simpler for personal use, with protected-folder search in the header, a clearer "Protection status" view, and advanced tools tucked into a collapsible Settings section.
Unmounting is safer and easier to understand: every unmount now asks for confirmation first, and a new Mount session card shows what is still pending before you stop a folder.
important_changes: Files just created in a Finder-backed protected folder can now be renamed, edited, and moved right away, because the app resolves newly created items to their stable identity.
The folder view now leads with "Open mounted folder"; "Reveal encrypted source" and "Unmount folder…" moved into a ••• menu, with unmount marked as destructive.
Unmount warnings now include "Review mount details", showing pending encrypted commits, the oldest pending change, affected file paths, the underlying error, and what to do next.
Renaming or moving a protected file no longer leaves a duplicate encrypted copy behind: the previous encrypted file is moved into retention instead.
Terminal access, diagnostics, coverage commands, and "Unmount all" now live under Advanced tools in Settings, and backend and provider names moved into mount details.
macOS builds are now produced by a public release workflow, and the packaging script verifies signing identities before building.
fixes: Fixed Conflict Review showing a stale "conflicts cleared" message; it now refreshes mount status and clearly says when unmount is still blocked by other pending work.
Fixed the folder detail view jumping back to the top every few seconds while the missing-items list was being reviewed.
Fixed write-back retries so a file's identity is preserved when a pending change is flushed before the next scan.
Removed a duplicated Device center button and a duplicated unmount-safety statistic, and made zero-issue cards visually quieter.

highlights: macOS File Provider mounts are more reliable: the app and Finder extension now use a shorter app-group socket path that stays inside the shared container instead of falling back to a sandbox-denied temporary path.
Protected folders on macOS now wait for the Finder File Provider domain and bridge socket to become healthy before the desktop app reports the mount as ready.
important_changes: The macOS File Provider socket path now uses `~/Library/Group Containers/<team>.group.com.hybridcipher.macOS/<root>.sock`, removing the extra `s/` directory that could push paths over macOS Unix socket limits.

Desktop macOS mounts now verify File Provider domain visibility and runtime socket health before marking a protected folder as mounted, and fall back to sync mount when the File Provider runtime is unhealthy.
Unmount, logout, and quit flows now keep macOS File Provider roots running when pending provider work makes a clean stop unsafe.

macOS release tooling was clarified with `desktop_release_pkg.sh`, `local_test_build_macos_pkg.sh`, and a new local environment template for signing, notarization, updater keys, and public release metadata.
fixes: Fixed a macOS File Provider socket path issue that could prevent Finder-backed mounts from listing and hydrating files correctly.
Fixed desktop mount readiness so macOS File Provider roots are not marked ready until the Finder domain is reachable and the bridge socket passes runtime health checks.
Updated macOS File Provider evidence checks and documentation to match the new app-group socket location.

highlights: macOS desktop release builds now stage and validate the File Provider runtime inside the app bundle, helping installed builds keep Finder-backed protected folders available.
Desktop login is safer on macOS: Remember Me now keeps only the email address and removes any legacy saved password from local storage.
important_changes: The macOS installer now registers the bundled File Provider extension after install so protected folder mounts are ready for Finder integration.
Local macOS release packaging now refuses to publish an app when the File Provider extension is missing or has an unexpected bundle identifier.
Public macOS source-verification hashes were refreshed for the latest unsigned Apple Silicon and Intel desktop artifacts.
macOS desktop build dependencies were refreshed, including Tauri, Tauri plugins, reqwest, and AWS-LC.
fixes: Fixed a macOS release packaging gap where the File Provider runtime could be absent from the final app bundle.
Fixed macOS build issues caused by the legacy FUSE mount path by limiting FUSE mounts to Linux builds.
Fixed Remember Me password persistence in the desktop app while preserving email prefill.

highlights: macOS File Provider support is now built into the desktop app, giving protected folders a more native Finder-facing mount experience.
File Provider startup and restore flows are more resilient, with stronger runtime checks, persisted registration validation, and better lifecycle recovery.
important_changes: Desktop login and session restore now reconcile persisted macOS File Provider roots, restarting stale bridges or unregistering unsafe stale domains when needed.
The File Provider bridge now supports persistent provider state, stable item identifiers, directory-scoped enumeration, and explicit domain signaling for Finder updates.
Provider control and readiness checks are more complete, with register, unregister, signal, and status flows backed by clearer runtime diagnostics.
fixes: Fixed cases where protected folders on macOS did not mount or restore cleanly after app startup, login, or session recovery.
Removed a redundant mounted-folder action in the enrolled folders view, making the macOS folder controls clearer.

highlights: Auto-mount can now restore the last mounted protected folder after login, with a Settings toggle for users who prefer manual mounting.
Public source verification is clearer, with reproducible unsigned macOS build guidance and published hashes for comparing source-built artifacts.
important_changes: The desktop app now remembers the last mounted root safely in local storage and skips auto-mount when the folder is no longer enrolled or already mounted.
Update install UI is split into dedicated frontend methods, with clearer update badges, progress states, restart prompts, and manual update checks in Settings.
Restricted personal builds now explain that team and group administration commands are disabled instead of describing the whole client as individual-only.
fixes: Removed deprecated desktop shell-open and xterm package dependencies, reducing packaging noise and warning output.
Cleaned up Tauri command organization, CLI path handling, notification paths, and release-note loading fallback behavior for public desktop builds.

highlights: Coverage Center is now built into the desktop app so you can review folder coverage, scan progress, and attention items in one place.
Post-quantum protection status is clearer across the workspace home, folder detail view, and header badge.
important_changes: Protected-folder enrollment errors now classify common failures such as permissions, missing paths, and already-protected folders.
Mount progress and timeout messaging now identify the target folder and explain when backgrounding is available.
Force unmount now requires a typed FORCE confirmation before the destructive path can continue.
fixes: Refined empty states, action labels, and workspace copy around coverage and folder protection.
Improved mount and unmount safety guidance for conflict, recovery, and long-running operations.
